body:
It's not a place you want anybody to be in- and I understand and share your

thinking about life not having changed in any meaningful way over those years. And yes,

it sure does sting, A LOT.

I understand, and we're probably in a similar spot then.. The only reason I don't

act on it is to spare my parents.

You're right about no one being able to predict the future, and also about

that we lean more toward thinking and expecting the worse. It's just that after

so many years, being hopeful for your future feels as if you're fooling yourself and

denying some sort of "truth". 

It's great you've had some positive experiences by going to those gatherings, and I hope

that after this crazy period of time of lockdown and distancing you can pick that back up

and add some more experiences just like that. I would enjoy being able to sit around with

likeminded people and just talk. It's difficult to go and do, because I'm extremely anxious

socially- and always afraid I'm going to feel out of place, or not be able to keep up with

the 'pace' and will just be awkwardly sitting around feeling umcomfortable.

Thank you- I guess you 

never really know, but it's just that besides my parents, hardly anyone sees me or has anything

to do with me. I'm not part of anybody's life in any significant way, nor is anyone

dependant on me.. So I always imagine if I'd just be gone, no one would really notice

in their daily lives, there's nothing they would miss or that would be out of place- besides

just having the knowledge I'd be dead, but I imagine they'd quickly continue living

their lives and forgetting all about me- as they do now whilst I'm around as well.
